title: Change a hearing aid's zinc-air battery with a battery magnet
instruction: Change the hearing aid's battery. Hold the aid in one hand and handle the cells only with the battery magnet. When you finish, the old cell and the new cell's pull tab are in the used-battery cup, the new cell is in the door with its + side to the door's + mark, and the door is clicked shut. Don't drop anything, and let go of the aid.
context: Many hearing aids, behind-the-ear models among them, run on size 13 zinc-air cells changed every 5 to 14 days: tens of millions of changes a year in the US alone. For older users with poor sight, tremor or arthritis the 7.9 mm cell is a known barrier, so family carers and care-home staff take the job over; an assistive home robot that can do it keeps the aid in use. Makers tell users to peel the cell's tab, insert it + side to the door's + mark (a battery magnet helps) and close the door. Here a cell too small for a gripper moves only on the magnet and is released by sliding the tip off against a wall, while the other hand holds the 6 g aid and a detented door is worked through its pull tab.
fidelity: 240 Hz rigid bodies. Door: a pin joint; a detent rule switches its spring (about 0.75 N at the tab to open or click). Magnet: a hold, not a field: a cell within 1.5 mm under the tip is kept on it with at most 0.25 N (0.15 N across the face), and let go beyond. Tab: a fixed joint that breaks at 0.4 N; collider 0.8 mm thick (real film about 0.15 mm). Cells 3 g (real 0.8 g), door 2 g (real about 1 g).
setup: Both arms empty, grippers open, at the station's ready pose. Positions in the station frame (m; x forward, y to the robot's left). A grey silicone mat (260 mm along x by 300 mm along y, 3 mm thick) taped to the table, centred at (0.29, -0.04); everything else stands on it, each item's outline drawn on the mat. Hearing aid: Sharper Image Digital Behind-the-Ear Hearing Aid (OTC, size A13 zinc-air cell, swing-out battery door; beige ABS; about $40), lying on its side, long axis along y, battery door at its right (-y) end, ear hook at the left, middle of the body at (0.36, 0.04). Modelled body 36 x 13 x 11 mm, 6 g; door pinned at the far (+x) corner of the right end, swinging out past that end up to 95 deg, a 5 x 1.5 x 3.5 mm pull tab on its free corner, a cradle 9.6 mm across (3 mm wall) over a lip with a 6.4 mm hole (measure and record the real aid's sizes). Door held shut by its detent: about 0.75 N at the pull tab to open, about 0.75 N over the last 6 deg to click shut; once open, the pin's friction holds it (about 0.3 N moves it); measure with a 0-5 N push gauge and record. In the door, shut: a used size 13 cell, + side up (toward the door's + mark). Cells: Duracell Activair EasyTab size 13 (orange tab; 7.9 mm x 5.4 mm, 0.8 g); one new cell per trial. Its dial pack (plastic dial on a card backing, about 48 mm across, 5 mm thick) lies flat, centred at (0.25, 0.00), its open pocket (9.4 mm across, 2 mm deep) at the dial's centre, holding the new cell + side up, its long pull tab (6 x 14 mm) folded straight up at the cell's left (+y) edge. Battery magnet: a standard hearing-aid battery magnet with brush (plastic, 8 mm flat-sided shaft, 5 mm magnet face on a 12 mm neck, 81 mm from the face to the brush; measure and record), standing magnet down in the 9 mm hole of a 40 x 40 x 25 mm plastic pen block taped at (0.20, -0.16). Used-battery cup: a 30 mL (1 oz) plastic medicine cup, about 40 mm across and 30 mm tall, taped at (0.26, -0.08). A phone 50 cm over the mat on its 3x camera films the trial (1080p).
scoring: Overhead phone video; a look at the door after. 1.0 when, with the hands clear for 1 s: the old cell in the cup; the new cell's tab off and in the cup; the new cell seated in the door's cradle, + side to the door's + mark; the door clicked shut (flush, and it stays shut when the aid is held door-down and shaken 3 times through 5 cm); both grippers and the magnet 3 cm or more from the aid. 0.5: all that, but the door shut to within 20 deg, not clicked. 0.25: old cell and tab in the cup, new cell seated + side up with its tab off, door open more than 20 deg. 0.1: door opened past 20 deg and old cell in the cup. 0 if a finger touches a cell, a cell lands on the mat or table anywhere but in the cup, the new cell lies in the door upside down or with its tab on at the end, the aid leaves the mat, or the aid is held or touched at the end. Anything else: 0.
reset_notes: Score first: in the video, check that no finger touched a cell and that no cell fell; check the door is flush, then hold the aid door-down over the mat and shake it 3 times through 5 cm: it must stay shut; open the door and photograph the cell (the + face is the flat face with the air hole) next to the door's + mark. Reset (about 2 minutes): take the new cell out with the magnet and keep it as a used cell; put a used size 13 in the door + side up and click it shut; lay the aid on its outline; tip the cup out; take a fresh cell from the pack by its tab, set it + side up in the open pocket and fold its tab straight up at the cell's left (+y) edge; stand the magnet in its holder. Tab check, once per box: tape a cell down by its - side, clip a binder clip to its tab, hang a paper cup from it and add coins until the tab peels; weigh (1 g steps): force = grams x 0.0098 N; 3 cells (the model takes 0.4 N). Spent zinc-air cells are harmful if swallowed: keep them in the closed cup and recycle them.
scores: Scripted demo: 1.0 (2,223 steps); Dream-1 run: 0.0 (valid run)
